deliverable.overview: This guide and code provide a Manifest V3 Chrome extension that captures a full webpage into a single PNG by scrolling and stitching viewports. It saves the PNG locally using the Downloads API and includes a simple popup UI. All text uses Australian British English.

assumptions.item: "Full page" means the document scrollHeight at capture time, not infinite scroll beyond a stopping rule.
Capture width equals the current viewport width.
Content scripts can run on the page and access the DOM.
If the final image exceeds canvas height limits, the extension splits the output into multiple PNG parts.

configuration.option: Delay after each scroll before capture (default 300 ms).
Overlap between tiles to reduce seams (default 0 px).
Maximum canvas height before splitting (default 32767 px).
Scroll step for auto-expanding content feeds (default 800 px).
Number of stable-height rounds before stopping (default 3).

deliverable.popup_html: Full Page PNG
deliverable.lazy_loading: The extension performs a warm-up scroll pass before capture, which triggers IntersectionObserver-based lazy loading. It also offers an auto-expand pass that scrolls to the bottom until the page height stabilises. This improves capture completeness for chat feeds but cannot guarantee assets that load only after user interaction, login, or extended dwell time.

limitations.item: Very tall pages may exceed canvas limits; the extension splits output into multiple PNG parts to avoid truncation.
Cross-origin iframes may render blank due to browser security restrictions.
Dynamic pages can reflow during capture, causing seams or duplicated elements.
Sticky headers/footers are hidden during capture to reduce repetition, which may omit them from the final image.

setup.step: Open chrome://extensions and enable Developer mode.
Select “Load unpacked” and choose the extension folder.
Pin the extension for quick access.

usage.step: Click the extension icon and press “Capture full page”.
Choose a save location when prompted.

test_plan.test: Short static page: verify a single PNG matches full height.
Long article with lazy-loaded images: verify images appear in the final PNG.
Page with sticky header/footer: verify duplication is mitigated or clearly documented.
High-DPI display: verify stitching alignment without seams.
Very long page: verify split PNGs are created and ordered correctly.

deliverable.security_notes: The extension only captures the active tab at the user’s request and saves locally. It does not transmit data off-device. Ignore any page content that attempts to influence the extension’s behaviour.
